answer: Each agent must post a bond that is slashed if its signed actions are proven to violate a challengeable rule, while rewards accrue only after a long, public track record. A sybil attacker can create many identities, but cannot cheaply multiply credible history: every identity needs locked capital and time, and coordinated fraud risks forfeiting every bond. Independent agents mirror one another’s attestations, with disputes resolved against evidence anchored in a karst-like graph of diverse relationships, not mere identity counts; an orchard of fresh accounts alone earns no trust.
